indian.headline: Indian markets closed lower on broad selling, with energy and metals leading declines amid inflation concerns.
indian.lead: Indian markets closed lower on broad selling, with energy and metals leading declines amid inflation concerns.
indian.brief: Sensex fell 0.47% and Nifty 50 dropped 0.52% as auto, metals, and energy sectors weakened, though pharma gained 0.7%.
why: Wholesale inflation hit a decade high of 12.29% in October on fuel and power costs, raising odds of an RBI rate hike in December and weighing on rate-sensitive sectors like autos and metals.
Energy stocks fell 0.9% and metals 1.9% as wholesale price pressures signal persistent cost headwinds for commodity-linked industries.
Pharma bucked the trend with a 0.7% gain, suggesting defensive buying as investors braced for monetary tightening ahead.
Banking held steady with just a 0.1% dip despite record Nifty Bank highs, as PSU banks like PNB and Canara gained 3–4% on strong Q2 results, offsetting broader market weakness.
indian.narrative:
Indian equity markets retreated on 18 November as broad-based selling gripped the session, with the Sensex closing 0.47% lower and Nifty 50 sliding 0.52%. The day's weakness was driven by mounting inflation concerns: wholesale price inflation jumped to 12.29% in October—the highest in a decade—on surging fuel and power costs, with Union Bank of India now warning that WPI could touch 11% in fiscal 2027. This sparked expectations of a 25–50 basis point rate hike from the RBI in December, pressuring rate-sensitive sectors. Auto shares fell 1.1% and metals 1.9%, the day's sharpest decliners, as investors worried about margin compression and slowing demand. Energy stocks dropped 0.9% on lingering oil-price anxieties linked to the RBI's record $239 billion forward book, which economists warn could keep the rupee under pressure.

Not all sectors capitulated. Pharma rose 0.7%, signaling defensive positioning ahead of potential rate hikes, while banking recovered from early weakness as PSU names PNB and Canara Bank surged 3–4% on robust Q2 FY27 earnings, lifting Nifty Bank to a fresh record high of 61,875. Bank Nifty itself eased just 0.06%, the smallest decline among the three main indices, suggesting institutional confidence in the sector's earnings trajectory. Meanwhile, brokerages like Motilal Oswal backed 25 stocks including Bharti Airtel and ICICI Bank but flagged a broader earnings slowdown ahead, with Nifty companies posting 27% profit growth in Q2—down from prior-quarter momentum. The session underscored a market bifurcated between defensives and cyclicals, with inflation the arbiter of sentiment.

tiles.sub: No explicit global drivers mentioned; rupee pressure from RBI's $239 billion forward book is an internal constraint.

tiles.sub: No fresh data on FII flows; broad market weakness and rate hike fears typically trigger FII outflows.

tiles.sub: WPI inflation driven by fuel costs; RBI's $239B forward book reflects rupee weakness on oil imports.

indian.watch: RBI's December policy decision and retail inflation print for October; any hint of a 25–50 bps rate hike could reignite selling in autos and metals.

us.headline: US markets closed lower across the board, with Financials hit hardest as tech earnings jitters weighed.
us.lead: US markets closed lower across the board, with Financials hit hardest as tech earnings jitters weighed.
us.brief: S&P 500 fell 1.03%, Nasdaq dropped 0.74%, and the Dow slid 1.64% as investors braced for major tech earnings and IPO news.
why: Nvidia earnings and Anthropic IPO looming: Tech stocks sold off as investors locked in gains ahead of heavyweight corporate events, dragging the Nasdaq down 0.74%.
Financial sector weakness: Banks and financial services fell 1.9%, likely tied to broader market caution and potential rate outlook concerns.
Intel shareholder crisis deepens: A 29% stock plunge and $140 billion value wipeout—plus ongoing lawsuits over hidden PC sales slowdown—fueled sector-wide chip stock anxiety.
us.narrative:
US equities finished in the red on 18 November as three major headwinds pressured investors. Tech stocks retreated 0.9% ahead of Nvidia's earnings report and Anthropic's planned IPO, triggering profit-taking across the sector. Intel's ongoing shareholder lawsuit over its catastrophic 29% single-day collapse—sparked by concealed PC sales weakness—cast a shadow over semiconductor sentiment. The Dow bore the brunt, falling 1.64%, while Financials tumbled 1.9%.

Meanwhile, some pockets of strength emerged amid the selloff. Berkshire Hathaway doubled down on homebuilder Lennar and raised its Delta Air Lines stake in Q3, signalling Warren Buffett's confidence in housing and travel demand despite near-term market jitters. Healthcare stocks also fell 1.4%, and Energy dropped 0.5%. The broader mood remained risk-off as the IMF warned of over-reliance on AI-driven investment, while Goldman Sachs predicted gold would need until end-2028 to reclaim its all-time high.
